input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my phone’s internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?
It’s just this one phone that’s having the problem, and the number is 555-123-2002. I only use this phone, so I hope that helps. What should I do now?

Looking at the top of my phone, I see some bars for signal, and it says 2G. There’s also something that looks like a little phone and a lock, and my battery is at 80%. I don’t see an airplane icon.

Is that okay, or is something wrong with it?

Oh, I definitely don’t know how to do that! Could you please give me the step-by-step instructions? I get nervous with these settings, so please go slowly. Will this mess up anything else on my phone? I really don’t want to lose my photos or anything important.
Okay, I followed your instructions, and now at the top of my phone it says 5G and the signal bars look full. Is that what we wanted? What should I do next?
I tried to do a speed test, but it says there’s no connection. That’s strange, because it shows 5G at the top now. What should I do? Is there something else I need to check?

I checked, and my mobile data is turned on, and my SIM card is active and working. There aren’t any error messages about the SIM card, and I’m not in airplane mode. Everything looks normal, but I’m still not getting a connection when I try the speed test. What should I do now?

I checked, and my APN name says “internet,” and there’s something about an MMSC URL too. I’m not sure what any of that means. Is that what it’s supposed to be, or do I need to change something? I just want to make sure I don’t mess anything up.

Alright, I’ve reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to restart my phone now—will that erase anything, like my photos or messages? I get a bit nervous about restarting. Can you reassure me before I do it?

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says there’s no connection. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working if everything looks fine at the top of my phone? What else can we try? I really need excellent internet speed.
I checked, and Data Saver mode is already off on my phone. So that doesn’t seem to be the problem. Is there anything else we can try? I really need to get excellent internet speed working.
Yes, please transfer me to someone who can help. I just want to get this fixed so I can have excellent internet speed. Thank you for trying to help me.

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my phone’s internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?

Thank you for reaching out about your mobile data issue. I can help you troubleshoot and improve your mobile data connection.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can check your account and guide you through the steps to resolve your mobile data problem.
My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?

Thank you, John. I have located your account using your phone number.

To help you fix your mobile data issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few steps on your phone. First, could you tell me if you are experiencing this problem on all your devices or just one? If it’s just one, please confirm the phone number of the device with the issue.

Once you confirm, I’ll walk you through some simple checks and fixes to get your mobile data working properly.
It’s just this one phone that’s having the problem, and the number is 555-123-2002. I only use this phone, so I hope that helps. What should I do now?

Thank you for confirming. Let’s start by checking your phone’s current network and data status. This will help us identify if there’s an obvious issue like Airplane Mode being on, poor signal, or mobile data being disabled.

Please look at your phone’s status bar (the area at the top of your screen) and let me know if you see any of the following icons:
- An airplane icon (✈️)
- A signal strength indicator (bars)
- A mobile data icon (like 4G, 5G, LTE, or similar)
- Any “no signal” or “x” symbols

If you’re not sure, I can guide you through a quick check using your phone’s settings. Would you like step-by-step instructions for this?
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Looking at the top of my phone, I see some bars for signal, and it says 2G. There’s also something that looks like a little phone and a lock, and my battery is at 80%. I don’t see an airplane icon.

Is that okay, or is something wrong with it?

Thank you for describing what you see. The fact that your phone shows “2G” is likely the main reason your mobile data is slow or not working well. 2G is an older, much slower network technology and is not suitable for fast internet or many modern apps.

Let’s try to improve your connection by switching your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, which should give you much better speed.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to change your network mode to 4G/5G, or do you know how to do this already?

Oh, I definitely don’t know how to do that! Could you please give me the step-by-step instructions? I get nervous with these settings, so please go slowly. Will this mess up anything else on my phone? I really don’t want to lose my photos or anything important.

No problem, John! Changing your network mode will not affect your photos, contacts, or anything important on your phone—it only changes how your phone connects to the mobile network for calls and data.

Here are the step-by-step instructions to change your network mode to 4G/5G:

1. Open the “Settings” app on your phone.
2. Look for a section called “Connections,” “Network & Internet,” or “Mobile Network.” Tap on it.
3. Find and tap on “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
4. Look for an option called “Preferred network type,” “Network mode,” or something similar.
5. Tap on it, and you should see options like “2G,” “3G,” “4G,” “5G,” or “4G/5G preferred.”
6. Select “4G/5G preferred” (or just “4G” or “5G” if that’s the only option).

After you make this change, your phone may briefly lose signal and then reconnect. Wait a moment and see if your phone now shows “4G” or “5G” at the top instead of “2G.”

Please let me know once you’ve done this, or if you have any trouble with the steps. I’m here to help!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
Okay, I followed your instructions, and now at the top of my phone it says 5G and the signal bars look full. Is that what we wanted? What should I do next?

That’s excellent, John! Seeing “5G” with full signal bars means your phone is now connected to the fastest available network, which should greatly improve your mobile data speed and reliability.

To make sure everything is working as it should, please try using your internet—open a website, stream a video, or use an app that needs data. Let me know if your mobile data is now working well, or if you’re still experiencing any issues.

If you’d like, I can also guide you through a quick speed test to check your connection quality. Would you like to do that?
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried to do a speed test, but it says there’s no connection. That’s strange, because it shows 5G at the top now. What should I do? Is there something else I need to check?

Thank you for letting me know, John. Even though your phone shows 5G, if the speed test says “no connection,” there may be another issue—such as mobile data being turned off, a SIM card problem, or a setting that needs to be adjusted.

Let’s check a few more things step by step:

1. Please check if mobile data is turned ON in your phone’s settings:
   - Go to “Settings.”
   - Tap “Connections” or “Network & Internet.”
   - Tap “Mobile Network.”
   - Make sure the switch for “Mobile Data” is turned ON.

2. If mobile data is ON, let’s check if your SIM card is working correctly:
   - Is your phone showing any messages about the SIM card (like “SIM not detected” or “SIM locked”)?
   - If not, that’s good. If yes, please let me know.

3. If everything above looks normal, sometimes a quick restart can help:
   - Try turning your phone off and then back on.

Please let me know what you find after checking these steps, and if you see any error messages or unusual icons. I’ll guide you through the next steps based on what you see.

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
Your SIM card is active and working.

I checked, and my mobile data is turned on, and my SIM card is active and working. There aren’t any error messages about the SIM card, and I’m not in airplane mode. Everything looks normal, but I’m still not getting a connection when I try the speed test. What should I do now?

Thank you for checking those settings. Your line is active, your SIM card is working, and your plan includes 15GB of data per month, so you should have access to mobile data.

Since you’re still not getting a connection, the next step is to check your phone’s Access Point Name (APN) settings. Sometimes, incorrect APN settings can prevent your phone from connecting to the internet, even if everything else looks normal.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to check and reset your APN settings? This process is safe and won’t affect your personal data or photos. Let me know if you’d like to proceed, and I’ll guide you through it.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked, and my APN name says “internet,” and there’s something about an MMSC URL too. I’m not sure what any of that means. Is that what it’s supposed to be, or do I need to change something? I just want to make sure I don’t mess anything up.

Thank you for checking your APN settings. The APN name “internet” is common, but the details—especially the MMSC URL—are important for your phone’s data and messaging to work correctly.

To make sure everything is set up properly, I recommend resetting your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. This is a safe process and will not affect your photos, contacts, or other personal data.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings? After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Let me know if you’re ready, and I’ll walk you through it.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Alright, I’ve reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to restart my phone now—will that erase anything, like my photos or messages? I get a bit nervous about restarting. Can you reassure me before I do it?

Rest assured, restarting your phone will not erase any of your photos, messages, contacts, or other personal data. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on, which helps apply the new APN settings and can fix temporary issues.

It’s a safe and common step in troubleshooting. Once your phone restarts, your settings and all your information will still be there.

When you’re ready, please go ahead and restart your phone. After it turns back on, try using your mobile data again and let me know if the connection is working. I’m here if you need any more help!

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried the speed test again, it still says there’s no connection. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working if everything looks fine at the top of my phone? What else can we try? I really need excellent internet speed.

Thank you for your patience, John. I understand how frustrating this must be, especially since everything appears normal on your phone. Since we’ve checked your network mode, mobile data, SIM card, and APN settings, and you’re still not getting a connection, let’s check one more thing: whether there are any restrictions or data saver settings on your phone that might be blocking your internet.

Could you please check if Data Saver mode is turned on? Here’s how:
1. Go to “Settings.”
2. Tap “Connections” or “Network & Internet.”
3. Look for “Data usage” or “Data Saver.”
4. If Data Saver is ON, please turn it OFF.

Let me know what you find, and if Data Saver was on, try your speed test again after turning it off. If it was already off, please let me know so we can continue troubleshooting.
Data Saver mode is OFF.

Since all the usual settings are correct and you’re still unable to connect, there may be a deeper technical issue with your line or device that requires advanced troubleshooting.
